name: The Chinese University of Hongkong - Shenzhen campus
overview:
Founded in 2012, the Chinese University of Hong Kong Shenzhen Campus has over 3,300 students. It is a renowned institution and ranks first places in:

  • QS ranking: 49 Global World Ranking
  • 10 Asian University ranking
  • 28th worldwide in Computer Science and Information Technology.


Nicknamed the "Chinese Silicon Valley," Shenzhen is located in the north of Hong Kong and is the seat of many multinational high-tech companies including Huawei, ZTE, Tencent, and TCL. This dynamic metropolis is based on the economic and social development of Hong Kong, Macau, and the Pearl River Delta region, and enjoys a spirit of innovation and high quality creative talent, thus providing a modern, cutting-edge university setting.

Ideally located between Longxiang Boulevard (Longgang District) and Dayun Park, the campus offers a pleasant environment for students who can enjoy an area surrounded by hills and a lake. A real city, the Shenzhen campus has restaurants and cafeterias, mini-markets, a gym, a bank, a clinic, etc.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Online application form (will be sent by your host university)
  • Copy of passport
  • 1x1 inches photo (a recent one within six months; full face with white background)
  • A copy of your transcripts in English (available on your intra)
  • Motivation letter in English
  • 2 letters of recommendation


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Receipt of the admission letter

The digital Acceptance Letter and the JW202 Form will be processed within approximately 6 weeks after you submit your online application. CUHK will email you the digital documents for you to apply for an X (study) visa.


3. Visa application (more information here)

You must take the necessary steps in obtaining a study visa type X1 upon receipt of the letter of admission and the form JW202 (sent to you by email). Please check this site for more information. Price: between 110 and 130€ (2025). You can also entrust the file to an agency by clicking here.


The X1 visa is an entry visa valid for 3 months from the date of entry into China. After your arrival, you must obtain a Chinese residence permit within 30 days of entering China.


The host university will assist you with visa conversion procedures, medical examinations, and obtaining the resident permit.

Related costs are the responsibility of the students (see estimated budget at the bottom of the page).


Please note:

  • For the latest information regarding visa application, you should contact your nearest Embassy/Consulate of China.
  • After you arrive in the Chinese mainland, the X visa for single entry cannot allow you to exit and re-enter the Chinese mainland. You must stay in the Chinese mainland until the Residence Permit is granted.


4. Insurance and Health

According to the regulations made by Chinese Ministry of Education, all the international students in China are required to purchase comprehensive insurance and the valid period should cover the duration of their studies. The insurance fee is CNY 400 for half a year and CNY 800 for one year (50-100€) Incoming exchange/visiting students cannot register at CUHKSZ without proof of sufficient insurance cover as required.


Please purchase the insurance package after you are officially accepted by CUHKSZ (in July for Fall Term, November for Spring Term, April for Summer Session). You don't need to choose the insurance package by yourself. Please log in with your passport information and you will find out the package is already chosen for you. 


If you plan to travel outside the Chinese mainland during your study, it is highly recommended that you should have other insurances to cover your travelling durations and destinations.


In order to be fully covered for medical care, we recommend that you take out international insurance as well. It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/chine

Note: it is advisable to register on the French registry established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


To receive the latest information (health, politics, etc.) please check the diplomatie.gouv website : Conseils aux voyageurs - Dernières minutes et alertes - Page 1 sur 1 - France Diplomatie | France Diplomatie


5. Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on China, click here.

Note that the partner university arranges a pick-up at the airport. Find out here.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

CUHK - Shenzhen has rooms on campus. The bedrooms are for 4 people. The bathroom is shared with other students.

You must contact the international relations department of the partner university (oalinbound@cuhk.edu.cn) at least one month before your arrival to reserve your room. The earliest check-in date is one day before the registration date. 

The fees are the following: CNY600/student/term (about 70€) with a deposit of CNY800/student (about 100€) and it is refundable if there is no damage to the room when the students check out.


Notes:

  • On-campus accommodation is available to incoming exchange/visiting students but cannot be guaranteed due to limited capacities.
  • The colleges offer a 24/7 reception service. 
  • The colleges do not offer beddings. Please take that into account for your budget.
  • The above expenses should be paid in cash, China UnionPay Card, WeChat Pay or Alipay.
courses:
Credits

You must complete 30 local credits in order to validate Tech 4 internationally.


Academic calendar

You will have to arrive at the end of August to start your year (especially for getting accommodations).

Classes start early September and run until mid-May.


Department and courses

You will take courses within the Bachelor - Computer Science & Engineering program, and will also have access to some business classes in the School of Management & Economics.

Below is a list of courses offered by the university and validated by Epitech.


In the Computer Science & Engineering Program:

  • CSC 1001 - Introduction to Computer Science: Programming Methodology
  • "This course introduces the basics of computer programming using Python. Students will learn the basic elements of modern computer systems, key programming concepts, problem solving and basic algorithm design. The key topics include the basic Python language syntax, data types, operators, flow control, defining and using function, I/O, data structure and algorithms, and the basics of object oriented programming. This course provides a foundation to further study in advanced computing topics."
  • CSC 3001 - Discrete Mathematics
  • "This course introduces the relevant mathematical concepts and techniques in computer science with emphasis on proofs and rigorous reasoning. Topics include: logics, methods of proofs, recursion, elementary number theory, graph theory, counting."
  • CSC 3050 - Computer Architecture
  • "Introduction of the major components of a computer system, including instruction set architecture (ISA), CPU datapath, control unit design, pipelining, memory hierarchy, peripheral interfaces, and multiprocessor architecture. RISC-V architecture will be used as a reference architecture."
  • CSC 3150 - Operating System
  • "To introduce the basic architecture and functions of operating systems. By looking at the overall architecture and individual components of different types of operating systems, major design issues, algorithms and design trade-off are discussed."
  • CSC 3185 - Introduction to Multimedia Systems
  • "This course is to study the fundamental multimedia concepts. Topics include multimedia data representation and operation, multimedia data compression, JPEG and MPEG compression standards, multimedia communications, and multimedia system. In this course, students will learn the principles of multimedia technologies, and will gain hands-on experience in applying various medias in the application."
  • CSC 4005 - Parallel Programming
  • "This course introduces concepts of parallel programming. Topics include parallel computer architectures, parallel programming languages, data structure designs for efficient parallel processing, synchronization controls, and applying parallel programming to high performance computing and AI/Machine Learning."
  • CSC 4160 - Cloud Computing
  • "Topics covered include principles of cloud computing, cloud systems architecture, virtualization techniques, cloud services, big data analytics, cloud programming toolkits, and specific cloud applications. We will study some public or private clouds and application tools; such as the AIRS cloud built on CUHK-SZ campus, Amazon AWS, and Aliyun, etc. Cloud programming tools are introduced with Python, Hadoop, Spark, TensorFlow, etc. We emphasize the interactions between existing clouds, Internet of Things, mobile networks, edge clouds, machine learning, and artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) applications."
  • CSC 6001 - Analysis of Algorithms
  • "This is an intermediate algorithms course with an emphasis on teaching techniques for the design and analysis of efficient algorithms, emphasizing methods of application. Specifically, the topics include recurrence relation, divide-and-conquer strategies, dynamic programming algorithms, greedy algorithms, theoretical complexity analysis, approximation algorithms, trees-based algorithms, string processing algorithms, and graph-based algorithms and algorithms."
  • CSC 6032 - Advanced Operating System
  • "This course will present an overview of some advanced operating systems and their underlying design principles. Issues discussed will include virtualization techniques for virtual machines and containers, memory management on GPU, I/O management for GPU, and file systems for GPU. Each enrolled student will be asked to design an OS for such systems."
  • CSC 6051 - Image Processing and Computer Vision
  • "A picture is worth a thousand words. How does a computer 'see' and 'understand' a picture? This course is an introductory graduate level course to answer such questions. We will first cover principles of image formation, operations to alter images, feature extraction and other image processing methods to turn images into abstract descriptions. We will then turn to computer vision topics that discuss how to perceive the structure and semantics of the world, including multi-view geometry, structure from motion, and visual localization and recognition. We will also touch upon related topics in machine learning which are widely used in computer vision."
  • CSC 6105 - Computer and Network Security
  • "This course aims to introduce important topics in computer and network security from an applied perspective. Topics include: (i) applied cryptography (e.g., cryptographic primitives, programming with OpenSSL), (ii) network security (e.g., unauthorized accesses, large-scale network attacks, firewall & intrusion detection systems), (iii) web security (e.g., HTTP session management and web attacks), and (iv) system security (e.g., buffer overflow, passwords, file system security), and (v) wireless security (e.g., WiFi security, wireless broadband network security). The course also discusses latest applied security topics according to the current research trends."
  • CSC 6115 - Parallel Programming
  • "This course trains students to understand how to program a distributed and parallel computing system. Student will be familiar with parallel and distributed languages such as MPI, Pthread, OpenMP, etc., and use them to design parallel and distributed programs and applications."
  • CSC 6118 - Information Theory
  • "After introducing some classical information theory results, e.g., the source coding theorem and the channel coding theorem, this course covers various research topics that are closely related to information theory, including modern coding theory and network coding theory. This course also discusses how to use these theories for designing network systems."
  • CSC 6129 - Reinforcement Learning
  • "This course offers an advanced introduction to reinforcement learning. Bandit learning and Markov decision processes will be covered. The focus will be on the design, analysis, and application of algorithms for complex reinforcement learning problems. The course will cover some recent developments in the field. Students are expected to have experience with optimization, stochastic processes, linear regression, coding for numerical computation, and writing mathematical proofs."


In the Electronic Information Engineering program:

  • EIE3001 Signals and Systems
  • EIE4001 Introduction to Internet Engineering
  • EIE4007 Computer and Network Security
  • EIE4180 Network Software Design and Programming
  • EIE4190 Multimedia Coding and Processing


Epitech students can also access the following classes offered in the School of Management and Economics:

  • FIN2010 Financial Management
  • DMS2030 Operations Management
  • DMS2051 IT in Business Applications
  • MGT2020 Principles of Management
  • MKT2010 Marketing Management
  • MGT3010 Organizational Behavior
  • CSC1001 Introduction to Computer Science: Programming Methodology
  • CSC1002 Computational Laboratory
  • MGT4189 Entrepreneurship Practicum
  • MGT3210 Strategic Management
  • MGT4230 Innovation and Entrepreneurship
  • MGT3060 Quality Management and Innovation


Chinese lessons:

  • CHI1000I Chinese for International Students (3 credits, 42 study hours)


Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.)


Other Expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Medical insurance: 150€
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage
  • Visa: between 110-130€
  • Medical examinations in China: 50-100€
  • Residence permit application: 100€ (one year)
  • School supplies: 150€ (CNY 1,200).


Estimated budget

The local currency is the Yuan (RMB or CNY). 1 € = 8.26 RMB (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

Per month, we advise you to plan a budget of 300€ for your expenses.

  • Accommodation: 300€/year
  • Food: 200€
  • "The food is much cheaper here. Most of us eat at the self-serve cafeteria which costs about (for a hearty dish) less than 2.50 €. Meals off campus cost around 20-25 yuan, depending on what you eat and where you eat."
  • Transportation: 30€
  • Phone, internet ~15-30€
  • If you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes some roaming data in China, which can be very helpful for the first few days. Otherwise, you can easily buy a local eSIM or a China Unicom SIM card at the airport for short-term use.
  • Leisure: 100€

These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.
